reel.caption:
1% fee on ₹10 lakh: how much does it cost over 20 years?

Illustrative: ₹10 lakh growing at 12% a year for 20 years ≈ ₹96.5 lakh.
If a fee 1% higher cuts that to 11% a year, it's ≈ ₹80.6 lakh.
That 1% gap costs ≈ ₹15.8 lakh, more than the ₹10 lakh you put in.
A fund's yearly fee (its expense ratio) comes out of returns every year. Returns are not guaranteed.

Do you know your fund's expense ratio?

Sources: compound-growth maths (₹10 lakh × 1.12^20 vs × 1.11^20). Illustrative only.
